fact_label: Paraguay-source income test — physical work location, not client/payer location (Law 6380/2019 Art. 6)
value_raw: Paraguay's territorial IRP system draws its source-of-income line at WHERE THE ACTIVITY IS PHYSICALLY PERFORMED, not who pays or where a service is 'delivered.' Law 6380/2019 Art. 6's own text (confirmed directly against DNIT's official portal copy): 'Constituiran rentas de fuente paraguaya las que provienen de actividades desarrolladas en la Republica, de bienes situados o de derechos utilizados economicamente en la misma.' Genuinely foreign-sourced income (foreign dividends, foreign pensions, foreign capital gains, and work physically performed outside Paraguay) sits outside IRP's scope entirely. But a remote worker or consultant physically living and working from a desk in Asuncion for a foreign client is, on this test, generating Paraguay-source personal-services income -- taxed on the progressive 8-10% scale, itself exempt below roughly PYG 80 million/year (~$12,000) -- regardless of the client's nationality, location, or currency. Paraguay-sourced capital income is a flat 8%.
notes: CORRECTED 2026-08-23 after [specialist] verification return for revision on the 2026-08-22 original version of this row (our records) -- the original framed the Paraguay-source boundary around payer nationality ('a Paraguayan client') and delivery destination ('services delivered into Paraguay'), which is not what Art. 6 says and reads more favorably than the facts support for this feature's actual reader (a foreign national physically relocating to and living in Asuncion while billing clients abroad). Re-checked directly: fetched Art. 6's text from DNIT's own official portal (dnit.gov.py, Paraguay's tax authority -- primary-institutional tier, not aggregator paraphrase) and independently confirmed the physical-performance test both there and by re-reading the original cited source (paraguaysovereign.com/tax/territorial-tax-explained/), which itself states this plainly for exactly this reader: work 'performed from Asuncion may... be treated as local-source regardless of where the employer is located,' and 'do not assume 0% without professional advice' -- both points genuinely present in that source but omitted from the prior version of this row. Practical upshot for the headline 0% claim: it mainly protects passive/foreign-situs income (foreign dividends, pensions, capital gains) and work actually performed while physically outside Paraguay -- NOT the day-to-day remote-work case of someone sitting in Asuncion billing a foreign client, which this test places inside Paraguay-source scope. fact_label: Bank account access for foreigners — gated by residency, not by income type
value_raw: Paraguayan banks treat non-resident foreigners on a tourist entry or temporary migration card differently from residents -- the source's own language is that 'non-residents may face limitations,' not that account opening is impossible or categorically very hard (no source found this pass supports that stronger wording). Once a foreigner holds an actual residency permit and the resulting cedula (national ID), account opening is straightforward, and foreign-sourced income of any of the qualifying types (corporate/personal bank statements, brokerage/investment account summaries, rental agreements or contracts, audited financial reports, dividend certificates, tax filings or returns) is accepted as proof of funds without requiring local employment. With a cedula, both guarani and US-dollar accounts can be opened, and international SWIFT transfers are received with no exchange controls.
